item.title: FeedbackTrack: Visual-Cortex-Inspired Cross-Frame Feedback for Transformer Tracking
item.description:
Authors: Yueyang Cang, Xiaoteng Zhang, Zhiyuan Ning, Yuchen He, Li Shi

Visual object tracking requires effective temporal integration, yet most Transformer trackers still rely on predominantly feed-forward feature extraction. Existing temporal mechanisms typically update templates, prompts, queries, or prediction states, while intermediate representations are rarely reused to modulate corresponding processing stages. We propose \textbf{FeedbackTrack}, a visual-cortex-inspired framework that introduces sparse, group-level layer-aligned cross-frame feedback into pretrained Transformer trackers

item.description:
Authors: Pinli Wang, Yue He, Peng Cui

item.title: Generalized Convexity and Smoothness via Conjugate Duality: Optimization Theory for Deep Neural Networks
item.description:
Authors: Binchuan Qi

Deep neural network (DNN) training with stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and its variants achieves strong empirical performance, yet classical optimization theory does not fully explain this success. This limitation arises because conventional analyses rely on assumptions such as differentiability, convexity, or smoothness, which are often violated by DNN objectives. In this paper, we establish a unified optimization framework for DNN training by generalizing classical convexity and smoothness through Legendre functions and convex conjugation

item.title: Distributed Optimization with Streaming Data: A Temporal Weighting Perspective
item.description:
Authors: Muhammad Faraz Ul Abrar, Nicolò Michelusi, Erik G. Larsson

Optimization theory is a widely used tool for intelligent decision-making. While classical optimization deals with fixed, time-invariant objective functions, many modern applications operate in dynamic environments where data arrive sequentially, and the learning objective evolves over time, often under decentralized data and communication constraints. Motivated by these trends, we study decentralized optimization from streaming data through a structured time-varying formulation in which the global objective is a temporally weighted average of losses observed across the network

item.title: Deep Learning Imputation of Missing Radius of Maximum Winds (Rmax) Values in Tropical Cyclone Best-Track Data
item.description:

item.title: Model Discovery Agent: LLM-assisted Bayesian experiment design for data-efficient discovery of mechanistic world models
item.description:
Authors: Kevin Murphy

Predicting the answer to interventional ``what if'' questions --- the outcome of an action never taken --- requires a \emph{mechanistic}, causal model, not a curve fit; and learning such a model requires \emph{experiments}, because passive data leaves its mechanisms unidentified. Experiments are expensive, so the central problem is \emph{data efficiency}. item.title: RynnValue: Scaling Robotic Value Foundation Models with Temporal Distance
item.description:
Authors: Dongchi Huang, Hongyin Zhang, Bohan Hou, Siteng Huang, Zhian Su, Hang Guo, Tong Lu, Zhaofeng Xu

General-purpose reward models are increasingly the bottleneck for scaling robot learning, yet the recipe for learning value-related capabilities from large-scale heterogeneous corpora remains underexplored. Existing approaches tie supervision to task-internal anchors such as preferences or normalized progress, none of which transfer cleanly across embodiments and data sources. We introduce RynnValue, an open-source value foundation model for robotic manipulation that replaces these anchors with temporal distance, the directed cost-to-go from an observation to the language-specified goal

item.title: Financial Numerical Prediction and Allocation as Token Generation
item.description:
Authors: Xu Ouyang, Moontae Lee

Financial prediction typically relies on task-specific regression, ranking, or policy heads, separating the language model from the numerical object ultimately evaluated. We investigate whether a causal language model can instead represent forecasts and decisions directly through constrained token generation. FinATOM introduces a unified, head-free interface for three-step stock-return forecasting and dynamic five-ETF allocation
